text.en:
Zoya drew a treasure map for her friends. "The treasure is in the park," she wrote. Nobody could find it.
Her brother added two numbers: how far across, and how far up. Now everyone found it in a minute.
"Maps need exact addresses," he said. "On the Earth, those addresses are latitudes and longitudes."

A globe is a model of the Earth. Imaginary lines drawn on it help us find any place exactly.
Lines of latitude run east to west and are parallel circles. The Equator is at 0° latitude. It divides the Earth into the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere.
Important latitudes are the Tropic of Cancer (23½° N), the Tropic of Capricorn (23½° S), the Arctic Circle (66½° N) and the Antarctic Circle (66½° S).
Lines of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole. The Prime Meridian is at 0° and passes through Greenwich, London. It and the 180° line divide the Earth into the Eastern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere.
A place is found where its latitude and longitude cross. India lies in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres, and the Tropic of Cancer passes through it.
Latitudes run east to west. The Equator is zero degrees and splits the Earth into northern and southern halves.
Longitudes run from pole to pole. The Prime Meridian is zero degrees and passes through Greenwich.
The Tropic of Cancer is twenty-three and a half degrees north. It passes through India.
A place is found where its latitude and longitude cross, like an exact address.

problem.en: India is north of the Equator and east of the Prime Meridian. In which hemispheres does India lie?

text.en: North of the Equator means the Northern Hemisphere.

why.en: The Equator separates north and south.

text.en: East of the Prime Meridian means the Eastern Hemisphere.

why.en: The Prime Meridian separates east and west.

text.en: So India lies in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres.

why.en: Both facts together give the answer.

prompt.en: Your friend asks why we need latitudes and longitudes when we have place names. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: Many places have the same name, but latitude and longitude give an exact position.
Ships and planes use them to find their way.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the lines are real lines on the ground.

points.en: Latitudes run east-west; the Equator is 0°.
Longitudes run pole to pole; the Prime Meridian is 0°.
Latitude and longitude together fix a place exactly.
